references.text: The Lord's judgment on the people of Israel: all who were counted from twenty years old and upward, and who grumbled against the Lord, would die in the wilderness.
Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun are the only exceptions allowed to enter the promised land.
The Lord's declaration that the entire wicked congregation would perish in the wilderness.
Joshua and Caleb are mentioned as the only survivors among the spies who explored the land.
Confirmation that none of the men from twenty years old and upward would see the land, except for Caleb and Joshua, who followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Moses reminds the people that no one from that wicked generation would see the good land, except Caleb.
Joshua son of Nun was to lead the people into the land as their inheritance.
Caleb reminds Joshua of the promise given to him through Moses and notes that he is still alive after 45 years in the wilderness.
The book of Hebrews refers to this generation that fell in the wilderness because of their unbelief and disobedience.
Paul uses the wilderness generation as a warning example—most of them did not please God and were scattered in the wilderness.
